validity.researcher_notes: Checked two independent, non-wiki, non-GEM sources describing this exact segment (Beni Suef→Abu Qurqas/Qorqas, 150 km, 32 in, completed mid-2007): (1) MEED 'Gasco pipeline on course' — states 'the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (Gasco) is overseeing the project' with Petrojet as main contractor and Enppi supervising construction, $63m first section Beni Suef→Abu Qurqas, completion scheduled 2007. (2) Oil & Gas Journal 'Egypt's Natural Gas Operations and Plans' — states 'the Beni-Suef/Abu Qorqas line is 150 km of 32 in. pipe with a capacity of 16 MMcfd... completed in mid 2007 at a cost of about L.E 545 million', built under 'Gasco's plan to supply the South Valley governorates'; separately describes Gasco (est. 1997) as the company that 'manages, operates and maintains the national gas grid and its facilities.' Both sources match the sheet's LengthKnownKm=150 and Diameter=32in exactly — strong corroboration these describe this same segment, and both independently attribute construction/operation to Gasco, not to any Upper-Egypt LDC. Separately researched 'Nile Valley Gas Company' (NVGC): per Gulf Oil & Gas and TAQA Arabia / Egypt Oil & Gas company profiles, NVGC is a private local distribution company (LDC, a Taqa Gas/Taqa Arabia subsidiary) granted an EGPC franchise in 1998 to distribute natural gas to end consumers (households, industrial/commercial customers, CNG stations) across Upper Egypt governorates from El Wasta to Aswan — a downstream distribution franchise layered on top of the national transmission grid, not the builder/operator of the 32in transmission trunk line itself. The wiki appears to have conflated the region's distribution franchisee (NVGC) with the transmission-segment operator (Gasco). Sheet's blank Operator was incomplete but not as wrong as the wiki's specific claim; recommend filling with the verified correct entity.
